source:
Backyard Monsters is one of the most underappreciated strategy games ever made. It combined Clash of Clans, Factorio, tower defense, RTS, and idle progression years before most mobile games. The core loop was: build a monster base, gather resources, research new monsters, attack other players, and defend your own base while upgrades continued in real time.
I actually think a Roblox spiritual successor could be bigger than the original, because Roblox solves many of the social and multiplayer limitations that Facebook games had.

The Fantasy
You're not building a town.
You're growing a monster civilization hidden inside a suburban backyard.
Imagine:
 • gigantic mushrooms
 • monster nests
 • slime rivers
 • tree forts
 • toy blocks
 • abandoned bicycles
 • sprinklers become rivers
 • garden hoses become bridges
 • sandbox becomes a desert biome
The world feels gigantic because you're tiny.

Core Gameplay Loop

Login

↓

Collect resources

↓

Upgrade buildings

↓

Breed new monsters

↓

Scout nearby players

↓

Attack enemy bases

↓

Steal resources

↓

Expand territory

↓

Unlock stronger monsters

↓

Repeat

Every mechanic feeds this loop.

The base is your kingdom.

Battle Gameplay
Here's where I'd improve massively.
Old Backyard Monsters was mostly click-and-watch.
Instead...
Hybrid RTS.
Player
Drops monsters.
Can
Ping targets.
Cast spells.
Retreat.
Use abilities.
Activate ultimate.
Enough control to feel involved.
Not enough to overwhelm.

Base Defense
Every base should feel unique.
Defenses include
Spike traps
Acid pools
Tesla towers
Slime launchers
Monster dens
Poison flowers
Giant Venus flytraps
Rocket squirrels
Laser garden gnomes

Terrain Matters
Huge improvement.
Height matters.
Trees block vision.
Water slows.
Mud traps.
Sprinklers flood.
Tall grass hides units.
Sandbox slows heavy monsters.
Terrain creates strategy.

AI Behavior
Instead of dumb pathfinding.
Each monster has priorities.
Tank

Attack nearest defense

Protect allies

Taunt

Assassin

Ignore walls

Jump inside

Kill defenses

Escape

Healer

Heal lowest HP

Retreat

Makes every monster feel alive.

Exploration

I'd add PvE.

Seasons

Rain
More Goo.
Winter
Frozen rivers.
Summer

Autumn
Leaf camouflage.

Alliances
Neighborhood Monster Clubs.
Members

Share resources.
Raid bosses.
Alliance wars.
Alliance tech tree.
Alliance fortress.

PvP
Three modes.
Raid
Steal resources.
Ranked
Lose/gain trophies.
War
Alliance vs Alliance.

Reputation
Instead of trophies only.
Neighborhood Reputation.
Higher reputation unlocks
NPC traders.
Legendary bosses.
Special cosmetics.
Elite players.

Endgame
Not just bigger numbers.
Players chase
Monster encyclopedia completion
Perfect mutations
Rare decorations
Alliance rankings
Seasonal leaderboards
World bosses
Legendary base skins

Live Events
Weekly
Meteor crashes.
Alien invasion.
Backyard flooded.
Neighborhood barbecue.
Halloween monsters.
Christmas toy factory.
Every event changes gameplay.

Idle Progression
Offline
Resources continue.
Research continues.
Breeding continues.
Monster healing continues.
Expeditions continue.
Enough idle to respect players' time, but not so much that active play feels unnecessary.

Roblox-Specific Improvements
This is where a clone can become something much larger.
Instead of every player living in an isolated instance, imagine an entire persistent neighborhood server with 20-40 players.
Each player owns one backyard, but everyone can:
 • Walk to neighboring yards.
 • Watch live attacks.
 • Trade monster DNA.
 • Visit alliance fortresses.
 • Participate in neighborhood events (like defending against a giant cat invading multiple bases).
This makes the world feel alive in a way the original never could.

Technical Architecture

Server
├── Persistent World
├── Base Simulation
├── Resource Production
├── Combat Engine
├── Pathfinding
├── AI Behavior Trees
├── Research System
├── Alliance System
├── Matchmaking
├── Economy
└── Live Events

Client
├── Building Mode
├── RTS Controls
├── Combat VFX
├── Monster Animation
├── UI
├── Camera
└── Audio

Each player's base is an independently simulated "island" within the larger neighborhood, allowing efficient server performance while still supporting social interactions and live events.

Long-Term Retention
The best strategy games always have goals on multiple timescales:
 • 5-minute session: Collect resources, queue upgrades, check breeding results, attack one nearby base.
 • 30-minute session: Explore a new biome, defeat a boss, redesign your defenses, experiment with a new army composition.
 • Weekly goal: Complete alliance events, unlock a new monster family, climb ranked PvP, finish research branches.
 • Monthly goal: Earn limited seasonal monsters, evolve Ancient monsters, upgrade your fortress, and compete for neighborhood dominance.
The original Backyard Monsters proved that combining base building, asynchronous PvP, and long-term progression was compelling. A modern Roblox version could push that much further by emphasizing collectible monsters with unique AI, exploration beyond the home base, cooperative neighborhood gameplay, and a living world that changes through seasonal events rather than simply recreating the original formula.

answers.ask: Should we build one backyard base first, or the whole neighbourhood world map? Eight expanding world tiers will not fit in a single top-down image, so they would be separate maps.
answers.answer: Build one backyard base first as the playable vertical slice. The wider world map and its expanding tiers can come later as separate maps.

answers.ask: Are the neighbouring players' yards inside the same map as yours, or separate instances you travel to?
answers.answer: Neighbouring players' yards should be separate instances you travel to for scouting and raids, keeping each base focused and readable.

scene_prompt: Create a 3D top-down strategy map for one playable monster civilization base hidden in a suburban backyard, viewed at tiny-creature scale. Center the layout on a Monster Heart, with clear buildable territory branching outward for monster nests and housing, resource extractors and storages, laboratories, breeding caves, spell towers, defensive walls, turrets, traps, acid pools, slime launchers, poison flowers, Venus flytraps, and a future fortress footprint. Surround the base with oversized backyard terrain and landmarks: gigantic mushrooms, tall grass, trees and tree forts, slime rivers, a sprinkler-fed water channel, garden-hose bridges, toy blocks, abandoned bicycles, broken toys, soda cans, old tools, and a sandbox forming a small desert biome. Use height changes, mud, water, cover-providing trees and grass, and open approach routes to shape the terrain. Keep this yard as a focused standalone base map; neighboring player yards are separate destinations rather than visible plots in the same scene.
blob:
### Genre
The dominant genre is Strategy, with Simulation as a secondary influence for the persistent base-building and resource-production loop. Strategy owns the layout because this vertical slice is a player-built defensive base rather than a social neighborhood or an exploration map.

### Shape and preset
Use `terrain-open`, matching the Real-Time Strategy preset: one contiguous backyard battlefield where building territory radiates from a defensible core. Retain that preset’s open placement logic, but adapt it from opposing medieval bases to one monster civilization base; this is a focused home yard, not a symmetrical battle map.

### Config requirements
Use `tracker-core` as the central Monster Heart, visibly anchoring the civilization. Use `buildzone-plot` for broad, freely arranged buildable ground around it rather than fixed plot tiles. Use `cover-los` through tall grass, tree trunks, roots, mushrooms, and toy clutter that interrupt sightlines. Use `terrain-relief` for small rises, muddy dips, the sandbox dune area, and elevated tree-fort ground. Use `water-body` for the slime river and sprinkler-fed channel, crossed by hose bridges.

### Layout requirements
Place one `tracker-core` marker at the exact center of the defended territory, with all radial building sectors readable from it. Place `collectible-nodes` as several resource-extractor anchors around the outer buildable ring, kept outside the core’s immediate footprint and beside backyard debris, mushrooms, or terrain features; these support extraction without obscuring approach routes.

### Layout components
The central zone is the Monster Heart plaza, surrounded by dense nest, housing, storage, laboratory, breeding-cave, spell-tower, and future-fortress sectors. An outer defensive ring holds walls, turrets, traps, acid pools, slime launchers, poison flowers, and Venus flytraps, with open approach corridors between defensive clusters. Resource ground occupies the perimeter. Oversized backyard landmarks frame the yard: gigantic mushrooms, tall grass, trees and tree forts, toy blocks, an abandoned bicycle, broken toys, soda cans, and old tools. A slime river and sprinkler channel cut across one side, with garden-hose bridges; the sandbox forms a small desert biome on another edge. The boundary is implied by dense grass, roots, fences, and backyard objects rather than neighboring base plots. Compose it as a legible top-down radial base, with the Heart dominant and terrain approaches visible.

### Render order
Use `topdown`: the top-down plan is authoritative because readable building territory, defensive rings, resource anchors, and approach routes must remain spatially coherent for a strategy base.

### Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
Scale is medium: one dense playable backyard base at tiny-creature scale. Theme is whimsical dark-fantasy monster civilization inside an oversized suburban yard. Pipeline modifiers are `tiered` for the non-overhanging backyard relief and sandbox rises, and `CHECK` for the visible water channels; neither requires stacked-map capture. No P6 route validation is needed because this is open RTS terrain rather than a fixed lane.
